Stoczek Lukowski Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stoczek Łukowski, Poland

Demolished. Stoczek Łukowski was founded in 1547 under Magdeburg Law as bishops' property, and Jews were not permitted to live there until this status changed in 1805; the first records of Jewish settlement date to 1817. By 1939, 2,470 Jews made up 60 percent of the town's population. During WWII, Jews in the ghetto were deported to Parysów and then to the Treblinka extermination camp. This cemetery was partially destroyed during the war, and after it ended, residents stole all the remaining tombstones; only a single fragment of a sandstone matzevah, dated 1910, has since been found in the town.
